case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation
- Expect slow pier salmon fishing this week at all four ports. Pier ratings: **St. Joseph 1**, **Grand Haven 1**, **Muskegon 0**, **South Haven unrated** (no pier report).
- Go to **St. Joseph** if you want the pier. Its pier reports were the most positive, though they are weeks old.
- If you can get on the water, boats are doing better than the pier at Grand Haven, Muskegon and South Haven. Fish 40 to 90 feet down.
- If the pier is your only option, bring spoons and flies, and expect few fish.

## Why
- The pier reports are the weakest part of the picture: the newest pier reports (Grand Haven and Muskegon, Sept 7) were slow, and Muskegon reported no salmon from the breakwalls.
- The pier reports at St. Joseph (Aug 17) and Grand Haven (Aug 24) were only a step up, at "below average."
- I'd expect the pier to stay slow while surface water sits near 72 to 73 F. The buoy data showed no sharp drop that would signal an upwelling (the cold-water upwelling that pushes salmon to piers).

## Evidence
**Recent reports**
- Grand Haven, Sept 7: "The pier action was slow for salmon." (quality 0). Boats were fair, 40 to 120 feet of water, fish 40 to 85 feet down, on glow spoons and green or white flies.
- Muskegon, Sept 7: "No salmon were reported from the breakwalls." (quality 0). Boats were fair, 60 to 120 feet of water, fish 45 to 90 feet down.
- South Haven, Sept 7: no pier report. Boats had "pretty good fishing" (quality 3) at 110 to 120 feet, with the best water around 40 feet.
- St. Joseph, Sept 7: no pier report. Boats were below average (quality 1) at 100 feet, on spoons.
- St. Joseph, Aug 24: "There seemed to be a few fish around the piers" (quality 1). This report was from the buoy 45168 area, so its pier wording is not clearly tied to a pier catch.
- Grand Haven, Aug 24: "Pier anglers were catching a few coho salmon and steelhead, but the action was slow overall." (coho, pier, quality 1)
- St. Joseph, Aug 17: "The few salmon that were caught were all on spoons and spinners." (pier, quality 1)

**Past seasons**
- The similar-weeks search (surface water within 4 F of today's 72 F, within 21 days of Sept 13) returned only 2022 reports. No earlier seasons matched, so I have no history to add here.

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water this week: St. Joseph 73 F (-3 F over the week), South Haven 72 F, Grand Haven 72 F, Muskegon 72 F (each -1 F over the week) (buoy readings, measured).
- The conditions tool returned only buoy averages. Live data was not available, and it gave no modeled pierhead temperature or cold-layer depth, so I cannot say whether cold water is near the piers now.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension): mature Chinook in early fall tend to hold in water of 55 F or less, and upwelling brings salmon to piers. At 72 to 73 F, the fish are probably deeper, which matches the boat reports.

## Caveats
- The newest reports are from Sept 7, six days old, and this is early fall, when conditions can change quickly.
- Pier ratings rest on one or two old reports per port. South Haven has no pier report at all, so its rating is a gap, not a judgment.
- Live conditions were unavailable, so I could not check the pierhead water or any upwelling. Check the pierhead temperature before you go; a sharp drop would improve the pier.

## Sources
- Sept 7 bulletin (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32bbcf0
- Aug 24 bulletin (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3298204
- Aug 17 bulletin (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3288194
